items.title: ‘Surreal’: Emergency backup goalie from Mississauga gets second crack at NHL dream
items.summary: Mississauga’s Brendan Bonello can name every goaltender to suit up for the Toronto Maple Leafs over the last two decades. He also eventually realized his own quest to stop NHL shooters would likely never materialize. The Mississauga product patrolled the crease in junior and university hockey, along with a brief stint in the third-tier ECHL. His playing days over, Bonello got the opportunity to help the Maple Leafs’ organization whenever an extra netminder was needed at practice or a game-day skate. But with the NHL’s move to professionalize the seldom-used emergency backup position this season, Bonello and 31 other goaltenders are getting another crack at living out childhood dreams. “Your goal is to make it,” said the 27-year-old, who is serving as Toronto’s so-called “EBUG” in 2026-27 and grew up idolizing former Maple Leafs netminder Ed Belfour. “Getting a second chance, you don’t take it for granted. Calgary Flames emergency backup Dusty Nickel was in the same role the last five seasons before getting the permanent call. “Right place at the right time,” said the 35-year-old ex-Junior A goalie. ” Teams are now required to have EBUGs on rosters. The goaltenders, who travel with their club and wear No. 00, can’t have previously played in the NHL under a standard contract, must have 80 games or less of professional experience, and can’t have suited up in the pros over the three preceding campaigns.

items.title: Attack from behind on Toronto street ends with arrest of Mississauga man
items.summary: A Mississauga man has been charged with assault after a demonstrator was attacked from behind and punched several times in the head at a downtown Toronto event this past weekend, police say. Detectives with the Toronto Police hate crime squad said they arrested a suspect on Monday after a man turned himself in to police officers at 52 Division. m. last Saturday during a demonstration in the Yonge Street and Grosvenor Street area of downtown Toronto. “The victim was walking northbound on Yonge Street, near Grosvenor Street, and was engaged in a conversation with another demonstrator” when they were approached from behind by a man and punched “several times in the head without provocation,” police said in a news release on Wednesday. The victim fell to the ground as a result of the attack, police added. They sustained injuries to their face and leg. Investigators said a suspect surrendered to police at 52 Division in Toronto on Monday. A 20-year-old Mississauga man has been charged with aggravated assault in connection with the weekend attack. He was scheduled to appear in court at the Toronto Regional Bail Centre on Tuesday. The investigation is ongoing and anyone with relevant information is asked to call Toronto Police at 416-808-3505 or Crime Stoppers anonymously at 416-222-TIPS (8477).

items.title: Global retailer from China brings character-filled shopping experience to Mississauga
items.summary: A global retailer known for its affordable lifestyle products and character merchandise has opened a new kind of store in Mississauga, giving Canadian shoppers the first opportunity to experience a concept previously available only in China. MINISO opened its first international SUPER MINISO location at Square One Shopping Centre on Oct. 10, introducing a larger-format store that combines everyday products with collectible merchandise and displays dedicated to popular entertainment characters. The opening marks a new chapter for the retailer, which is expanding beyond its traditional lifestyle-goods format to put character merchandise and themed shopping experiences at the centre of its business. The 1,000-square-metre store features thousands of products inspired by licensed entertainment properties, alongside beauty products, fashion accessories, travel items and everyday essentials. One of the biggest draws for fans is the Canadian debut of the complete NARUTO × MINISO collection, along with the Stitch Hit Snooze Series. More merchandise featuring Hello Kitty and Friends, Marvel, Chiikawa, Mofusand and other popular characters is also planned, as is a growing range of products featuring MINISO’s own character, YOYO. Rather than simply placing branded merchandise on regular shelves, the SUPER MINISO concept uses themed displays and dedicated areas to make browsing part of the shopping experience. That approach is intended to appeal to fans who collect character merchandise as well as shoppers looking for practical, affordable products.

items.title: Mississauga Mayoral Candidates Lay Out Plans for Housing, Transit and Property Standards Ahead of Oct. 26 Vote
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports it asked mayoral candidates ahead of the Oct. 26 election how they would address housing affordability, declining MiWay ridership and rising complaints about littering and illegal dumping. According to the outlet, candidates were invited to answer two questions covering property standards enforcement and plans to improve transit access, speed and reliability. The outlet reports one candidate said the city needs more housing ordinary working families can afford, and pointed to faster approvals, purpose-built rental housing and better use of city-owned land as ways to grow the supply. Another response emphasized consistent, citywide enforcement of property standards with faster response times and transparent complaint tracking, rather than making residents repeatedly complain before action is taken. Mississauga.com reports candidates also described wanting MiWay to expand service where demand is demonstrated, improve frequency and connect underserved communities, arguing transit planning should follow where residents actually live and work.

items.title: Port Credit Ratepayer Groups Host Four-Way Mayoral Debate Ahead of Oct. 26 Election
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports the Town of Port Credit Association and the Lakeview Ratepayers' Association are hosting a resident-led mayoral debate on Thursday, Oct. 15, ahead of the city's Oct. 26 municipal election. According to the outlet, the debate will be held at Christ First United Church in Port Credit and is open to residents from across the city. The outlet reports four candidates, Bonnie Crombie, Dipika Damerla, Carolyn Parrish and Alvin Tedjo, are confirmed to participate, with discussion centred on property taxes, citywide intensification, transit and infrastructure. Mississauga.com says candidates will also field questions on provincial decision-making, strong-mayor powers and the city's provincial funding allocations. The outlet reports residents will get a chance to ask their own questions once the formal debate segment wraps up.

items.title: Lakeshore Art Trail Marks 25 Years With Its Biggest Mississauga Show Yet
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the Lakeshore Art Trail is celebrating 25 years with its annual Art Show and Sale this weekend at the Small Arms Inspection Building. According to the outlet, more than 40 artists are exhibiting at what organizers describe as the largest fine art show and sale in Mississauga, with ambitions to eventually match the scale of similar events in Toronto and elsewhere in the GTA. The outlet says the show moved to its current venue in 2022 in partnership with CreativeHub 1352, bringing together 24 artists under one roof for the first time after years of artists displaying work out of studios and local businesses across Clarkson, Port Credit and Lorne Park. Insauga.com reports that first year at the new venue drew more than 2,000 visitors, and organizers now expect attendance to top 4,000 over this year's two-day event. The event remains organized by an artist-run executive committee, the outlet notes.

items.title: 2nd suspect arrested in Mississauga road rage incident that ended in double stabbing
items.summary: A second suspect has been arrested in connection with a road rage incident that ended in two people being stabbed in Mississauga in August. Peel police announced the arrest in a news release on Wednesday. The incident happened in a parking lot near Dundas Street West and Parkerhill Road on Aug. m. Police said the occupants of two vehicles confronted each other, and two people ended up getting stabbed. They were later taken to hospital with serious injuries. One person, a 30-year-old man from Mississauga, was arrested shortly after the incident. He was charged with assault. Police said on Wednesday that a second suspect, 26-year-old Isaiah Myles from Mississauga, was arrested and charged with two counts of attempted murder. “This arrest represents another important step in the investigation,” Peel police Chief Nishan Duraiappah said in a statement.

items.title: Trillium Opens Full-Scale Hospital Room Mockups Ahead of New Mississauga Facility's 2034 Debut
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Trillium Health Partners is giving the public an early look at the future Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital through full-scale mockups of hospital rooms at its Trillium HealthWorks Experience Centre. According to the outlet, the new hospital will rise 22 storeys on the same site as the current Mississauga Hospital and is expected to be the largest hospital in Canada when it opens in 2034. The outlet reports the facility will include the Shah Family Hospital for Women and Children, described as the first dedicated medical facility of its kind in Ontario. Insauga.com says Trillium, which also oversees Credit Valley Hospital and the nearby Queensway Health Centre in Etobicoke, is holding open houses on Oct. 20 and Oct. 24 so residents can tour the mockup rooms in person. The experience centre is located just west of Dixie Road at 1225 Dundas St., the outlet reports.

items.title: Mississauga Ward 8 Hopefuls Weigh In on Ridgeway Plaza's Parking and Noise Complaints
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports five candidates running for the Mississauga Ward 8 council seat were asked how they would address ongoing parking, noise and safety concerns at Ridgeway Plaza ahead of the Oct. 26 election. According to the outlet, the plaza has become known for its concentration of Middle Eastern and South Asian restaurants and shops and has grown into a major cultural destination drawing visitors from across North America. The outlet says that growth has also made the plaza a focal point for debates over traffic congestion, parking and noise management. Mississauga.com reports candidates were specifically asked what steps they would take as Ward 8 councillor to manage those issues while still supporting local businesses and surrounding neighbourhoods. The outlet published candidates' emailed responses, edited for length and clarity where necessary.

items.title: Mississauga Seeks Volunteers to Bring Back Dozens of Neighbourhood Ice Rinks This Winter
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the City of Mississauga is calling on volunteers to bring back its Natural Ice Rinks Program for another winter season. According to the outlet, dozens of neighbourhood parks across the city rely on volunteer rink-keepers to build and maintain outdoor ice surfaces once temperatures turn cold enough, typically by late December or January. The city says anyone willing to help must be at least 14 years old and comfortable working outside in winter conditions, often in the evening after dark. Applications are due by Nov. 15, the outlet reports. Unlike larger indoor facilities, insauga.com notes these community rinks exist only because local volunteers show up to care for them through the season, giving residents free spots to skate or play pickup hockey at locations ranging from Celebration Square downtown to parks throughout the city's neighbourhoods. City officials describe the program as a longstanding winter tradition in Mississauga and across Canada.

items.title: Road Rage Clash on Dundas Street West Leads to Second Arrest in Mississauga Stabbing
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a second suspect has been arrested and charged with attempted murder in connection with a Mississauga stabbing that began as a road rage dispute. According to investigators, officers responded in August to a confrontation near Dundas Street West and Parkerhill Road after an argument between the occupants of two vehicles turned violent in a parking lot, leaving two people stabbed and taken to hospital with serious injuries. Police say a first suspect, 30-year-old Ali Halimi of Mississauga, was arrested at the scene shortly afterward and charged with assault. Investigators with the 11 Division Criminal Investigations Bureau say the second suspect, 26-year-old Isaiah Myles of Mississauga, was arrested on Oct. 1 and held for a bail hearing at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton. Peel Regional Police describe the arrest as an important step in an investigation they say remains ongoing, and ask anyone with information to contact the 11 Division unit.
